newsitem.title: USA: Fluor Daniel Fernald to settle suit for $8.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: Fluor Daniel Fernald to settle suit for $8.4 mln.

text.p: Fluor Daniel Fernald said on Thursday it has agreed to pay $8.4 million to settle a lawsuit filed against the company by William Watt, a former employee.

Fluor Daniel Fernald said it agreed to pay $3.7 million for the alleged violations about the cleanup of the Fernald site, $1.7 million in attorney's fees, and $3 million relating to Watt's separation from the company.
Of the $3.7 million, $2.6 million will be paid to the government as required by law, Fluor Daniel Fernald said.
Watt had claimed damages of more than $300 million for alleged violations of the False Claims Act, the company said.
Watt's claims against the company ranged from allegations concerning cost estimating methodology to assertions that Fluor Daniel Fernald sought government reimbursement for an employee pizza party.
The company said it defeated many of the claims, but elected to settle the remaining claims because it was too costly to litigate.
Fluor Daniel Fernald said the Justice Department had elected early on not to intervene in the case and added that the U.S. General Accounting Office exonerated the company on a number of charges.

In its statement, Fluor Daniel Fernald did not say whether it was a unit of Norwood, Mass.-based Fluor Daniel GTI Inc or Irvine, Calif.-based Fluor Corp. The company was not immediately available for comment.
A company spokeswoman later said Fluor Daniel Fernald is a unit of Fluor Daniel GTI.
The project was to remediate a former uranium production site in Ohio.
